description: KNa₄FeO₄ crystallizes in the orthorhombic Pbca space group. K is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of K-O bond distances ranging from 2.63-2.75 Å. There are four inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ trigonal pyramids that share corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with three equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra,  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.27-2.37 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.34-2.52 Å. In the third Na site, Na is bonded to four O atoms to form distorted NaO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent FeO₄ tetrahedra, corners with three equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids, and  an edgeedge with one FeO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.26-2.43 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.33-2.41 Å. Fe is bonded to four O atoms to form FeO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaO₄ tetrahedra, corners with two equivalent NaO₄ trigonal pyramids,  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaO₄ trigonal pyramid. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.88-1.90 Å. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to five Na and one Fe atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing ONa₅Fe octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 51-72°. In the second O site, O is bonded to one K, four Na, and one Fe atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OKNa₄Fe octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 54-70°. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to one K, four Na, and one Fe atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to two equivalent K, three Na, and one Fe atom.
